pages.intro:
Order Desk takes customer orders off your team's hands. You drop an order in, and it does the typing and the checking:

1. **Reads the order.** Emails, PDFs, spreadsheets and scans are all fine.
2. **Finds the customer** and matches each line to your product list.
3. **Applies that customer's rules**, such as full cartons only or a usual delivery day.
4. **Checks its own work** and flags anything it is not sure about.
5. **Asks a person**, who can approve the order, fix a line or reject it.

You stay in charge. Below is the path every order takes.
pages.title: Meet Order Desk

pages.description: Both lists are needed before Order Desk can take an order.
pages.intro:
Order Desk works from two lists: what you sell and who you sell to. Download the template, paste your rows in, and upload it. An export from your accounting or stock system works too, as long as the headings match.

You can load a list again whenever it changes. Rows are matched on the item code and the account code, so nothing is doubled up.
pages.title: Load your lists

pages.description: You can change this at any time on the Setup page.
pages.intro:
Choose how much Order Desk does on its own. Most teams start with **Check everything** and loosen it once they trust the results.

- **Check everything.** A person approves every order.
- **Check only problems.** Clean orders go through on their own. Anything flagged waits for a person.
- **Hands-off within limits.** As above, and Order Desk also settles small doubts itself: it accepts a product when exactly one fits, and assumes the selling unit when a line has none.

The three limits below apply to every choice. They are the guard rails: a large order, a new customer's first orders and the occasional spot check always go to a person.
pages.title: How careful should it be?

pages.description: Safe choices are already filled in. You can change any of these later on the Setup page.
pages.intro: Every business answers these a little differently. If you are not sure, leave them as they are.
pages.title: How should it handle orders?

pages.intro:
**Drop orders in.** Open Order Desk's **Files** tab and drop each customer order into the **Orders** folder. Each file becomes one order and Order Desk starts on it straight away.

**Answer when it asks.** An order that needs a person shows up under *Waiting for you*. You see what the customer wrote next to what Order Desk will send, with anything doubtful at the top. Then choose one:

- **Approve order.** It goes to the warehouse.
- **Fix a line.** Change the product, quantity or unit right there. Order Desk checks the order again and asks you once more. It remembers the fix for that customer.
- **Reject order.** Nothing is sent.

**Keep the lists current.** When products or customers change, load the new list on the Setup page. Delivery addresses and customers' own product codes go in the **Lists** folder on the Files tab.
pages.title: What your team does

pages.description: Already filled in with safe choices. Change these only if you need to.
pages.intro:
These are set for you and most teams never change them.

**Extra checks.** How far above a customer's usual quantity is worth a second look, how long the same PO number counts as a duplicate, whether substitutions are ever allowed, and what to do when a line has no unit.

**Budget and quiet hours.** How much AI the agent may use each month, and the hours it should not work.
